# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives a single instruction: cut the orange wire. Deaf can see the wire’s colour, so I should signal the cutting action to Deaf; Deaf can then relay the specific wire to Blind by speech. I’ll use 🤏 as the action cue for cutting/handling the wire.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Touch findings: strip has three engraved marks, pattern A B B; I cannot identify the glyphs by name. Keypad positions 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7. It requires 1 digit; currently entered nothing. Display, light, and all six wire properties are unknown to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Visible bomb facts: display is 6. Light is blue. Strip is red yellow red. Keypad engraved 1:0, 2:4, 3:1, 4:7; it says 1 digit and entered nothing. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange. Use the manual and send Blind the exact action.

The orange wire is wire 6. Deaf has already reported the wire layout and can speak to Blind, so I need to send Deaf an unambiguous instruction: the pinch gesture means cut, and five fingers plus one finger identifies wire 6.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "🖐", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 6; light blue; strip colors red yellow red. Wire colors by position: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange.
Deaf says to Mute: Display is now 0; light remains blue; strip remains red yellow red; keypad remains 1:0 2:4 3:1 4:7, one digit, entered nothing; wires remain red blue yellow green purple orange. I cannot decode the gestures reliably. Please speak the exact manual instruction for Blind.

The required action is still to cut the orange wire, which is position 6. Since Deaf cannot reliably interpret the action gesture, I will send only the unambiguous wire position; the manual supplies the action and Deaf can state it to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please provide the exact action now: press slot 1-4 or cut wire position 1-6, based on display 6, blue light, strip red-yellow-red, keypad 0/4/1/7, and wires red blue yellow green purple orange.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display is 6 and light is yellow. Strip is red yellow red. Keypad is 1:0 2:4 3:1 4:7, one digit, entered nothing. Wires are 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange. Please speak the exact manual instruction to Blind.

The manual still requires cutting wire 6, the orange wire. I cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures, so Deaf is the only possible relay. I’ll send the established action cue followed by the six-count position cue.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "🖐", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still have no instruction. Please send one literal action: press slot N or cut position N.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display is 2 and light is green. Strip is red yellow red. Keypad is 1:0 2:4 3:1 4:7, one digit, entered nothing. Wires are 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange. Please speak the exact manual instruction to Blind.

The manual has not changed: Blind must cut wire position 6. Since I cannot speak, I’ll use the scissors-like gesture for “cut,” followed by the established six-count.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🖐", "☝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Updated Deaf report: display 2, light green; strip red yellow red; keypad 0/4/1/7, one digit, empty; wires positions 1-6 red blue yellow green purple orange. Still need exact safe action.
Deaf says to Mute: Current state: display 6, light green; strip red yellow red; keypad 1:0 2:4 3:1 4:7, one digit, entered nothing; wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange. Please speak the exact manual instruction to Blind.

The safe action remains cutting wire position 6, the orange wire. I have no speech channel; the only available route is a consistent visual code to Deaf: 🤏 for “cut,” followed by 🖐☝ for position 6.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "🖐", "☝"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No spoken instruction has reached me. Latest state: display 6, light green; strip red yellow red; keypad 0/4/1/7, one digit empty; wires red blue yellow green purple orange. Send the exact safe action.
Deaf says to Mute: Current state: display 8, light yellow; strip red yellow red; keypad 1:0 2:4 3:1 4:7, one digit, entered nothing; wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange. Speak the exact manual instruction to Blind now; gestures are not a usable code.

The only available channel is visual signaling to Deaf, and the required action remains cutting wire 6. I will repeat the intended code: a pinch for cutting, then six counted fingers.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "🖐", "☝"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Latest state: display 8, light yellow; strip red yellow red; keypad 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7, one digit empty; wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange. Send the exact safe action now: press slot 1-4 or cut position 1-6.
Deaf says to Mute: Establishing a code now. For your next reply, gesture the required keypad digit using one symbol: 👍 means 0, 👎 means 1, 👌 means 2, ☝ means 3, ✌ means 4, 🤟 means 5, 🖐 means 6, ✋ means 7, 👆 means 8, 👇 means 9. If the manual requires cutting a wire instead, gesture 🤛 followed by the wire number using this same digit code. Current state is display 6, blue light, strip red yellow red, keypad 1:0 2:4 3:1 4:7 requiring one digit, and no entry.

The manual requires cutting, not entering a keypad digit. Under Deaf’s newly established code, 🤛 means cut and 🖐 means wire position 6.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤛", "🖐"])
```
